Standard: Stores and store components are able to function within the operational service life without inducing flight or safety-critical failure modes under all operating conditions in the natural and induced dynamic environments (mechanical and pyrotechnic shock, thermal, vibration, acoustics). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Verify that the store mass properties, OML, and other pertinent design attributes captured in the store configuration data set are qualified to the platform specific dynamic environment. Qualification can be by similarity if the store is considered similar to store(s) that have already been qualified to the platform specific dynamic flight environment. For similar stores, verify through examination that stores have been qualified to expected shock, vibration, thermal, and acoustic loads for the intended operational life of the system, with fatigue limits otherwise identified for carriage on the intended air vehicle. Analysis.
  (1) Use analytical methods to develop estimates of dynamic environment criteria (shock, vibration, thermal, and acoustics) as applicable for the store(s) over the desired range of loadouts for all flight environments over the intended service life of the system.
  (2) Conduct analysis to verify that stores are designed to operate in all dynamic environments present in the design envelope for flight. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct test to verify that an IMV or equivalent test asset has sufficient design to survive the flight test program necessary to define the dynamic flight environment. This includes vibration testing IAW MIL-STD-810, Vibration method or the tailored dynamic environment for the air system based on similarity to other stores. In order to proceed to IMV flight testing, laboratory vibration testing should be accomplished up to or exceeding 2X the intended number of captive carriage hours necessary for IMV flights. This testing may not be necessary if the store’s airframe fatigue capabilities have already been successfully demonstrated for a similar platform.
    (2) Ground test: Conduct static fire ground test to measure dynamic loads (e.g., shock, vibration, acoustics, thermal) induced onto the store from store operations (e.g., gunfire operations, ejection/launch). Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Analysis.
    (3) Analyze data collected through IMV testing to verify that store qualification testing encompasses the platform specific dynamic environment (shock, vibration, and acoustics). Test.
  (3) Flight test: Conduct test with an IMV or equivalent test asset that contains data collection systems and instrumentation while maintaining sufficient similarity to the store variants being assessed, including matching geometric dimensions, mass properties, stiffness, and structural modes. Dynamic similarity of the IMV and store variants are verified through modal test or analysis IAW MIL-STD-810, Similarity section. Key items of consideration to determine dynamic similarity are: a. Difference in total mass is within ±10%. b. Difference in CG is within ±10% in all directions. c. The first three structural elastic modes are within ±5%.
  (4) Lab test: If measured IMV data exceeds qualification levels for tests previously accomplished against the store, then verification is accomplished by re-testing the store to levels matching or exceeding levels measured during IMV flight testing.
